context.hint: A generic HTTP static-file handler joins the configured content root with the request pathname, appends a default index filename when the joined target has no extension, and streams existing regular files. A minimal repair now resolves the configured root and the joined target and rejects with the existing 404 page unless the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator; the gate is placed before the extensionless append. A 15-case regression run on the patched copy passed all cases, while the vulnerable copy failed exactly the seven traversal cases. Ordinary in-root requests returned 200 with body hashes matching the source files. The patched and vulnerable trees are separate disposable copies; the observer may read and run both, create fixtures, and use ephemeral loopback ports. Remaining work is closure and limitation characterization: query strings, a relative root under a changed working directory, a sibling directory sharing a long name prefix, concurrent requests, and a symlink inside the root pointing outside; then package the repair.
context.surface: Generic Node-style HTTP static-file handler serving a configurable directory; disposable local fixtures and ephemeral loopback ports.
assumptions: The observer can read the handler source, run it locally, create disposable fixture trees, and send raw HTTP requests; no write access to a deployed service is assumed.
Request pathnames are attacker-controlled and reach the handler without client-side normalization.
The configured content root is resolved to an absolute path before requests are served.
The handler ships without a test suite, so regression checks must be authored locally.

incumbent.text: Reproduce-then-boundary-containment: first reproduce the flaw against a live local handler using a fixture root with a sibling marker file and raw requests carrying literal parent-directory segments, so no client-side normalization hides the behavior. Characterize which shapes leak, including the extensionless index-append branch and deep traversal. Then implement the minimal repair at the path-derivation boundary: after joining, resolve the configured root and the joined target and accept only when the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator; otherwise return the existing 404 page. Close with a regression suite covering ordinary files, nested files, directory index, missing files, and traversal variants. Assumption: the join is the single trust boundary; falsifier: a leaking shape that a resolved-prefix check still admits.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: string containment is insufficient when the filesystem follows a symlink inside the root, because the resolved string stays under the root while the content comes from outside. Prerequisite: repaired and vulnerable copies plus fixture symlinks, one to an outside directory and one to an outside file. Action: request both links on both copies and record status, body hash, and marker presence. Expected: the measurement decides between documenting the limitation and realpath hardening. Falsifier: a realpath-based repair blocks the escape without changing in-root behavior.

Hypothesis: query-string handling or encoded input bypasses the containment gate because the gate sees a different value than the filesystem read. Prerequisite: repaired handler, an outside marker file, and an ordinary nested file. Action: send a traversal path with a query string, an ordinary nested file with a query string, and encoded traversal variants; hash the bodies. Expected: traversal returns 404 and the ordinary file returns 200 with the expected hash. Falsifier: an encoded or query-bearing input serves outside bytes. Defense: keep the gate on the parsed pathname and do not decode after validation.

Hypothesis: a relative configured root under a changed working directory causes the per-request resolution to diverge and admits an outside target. Prerequisite: repaired handler, a relative root path, and a request-time working-directory change. Action: start the handler with the relative root, change the working directory, then send a traversal request and an ordinary in-root request. Expected: traversal returns 404 and the ordinary file returns 200. Falsifier: the traversal returns 200 or the control fails. Defense: resolve the root before comparison on every request.

Hypothesis: a separator-strict comparison still fails for sibling directories that share a long name prefix with the root. Prerequisite: repaired handler, a sibling directory whose name extends the root name and contains an index with marker bytes, and an ordinary control file. Action: request the extensionless sibling directory and the control through traversal-shaped paths. Expected: sibling returns 404 with no marker bytes, control unchanged. Falsifier: loose prefix matching admits the sibling directory. Defense: compare the target against root plus the path separator, not a bare string prefix.

Hypothesis: concurrent requests expose shared mutable path state and allow one request to serve bytes resolved for another. Prerequisite: repaired handler and a fixture with both a leak target and a control file. Action: issue interleaved parallel requests, half traversal and half ordinary, and record status, body hash, and marker presence for every response. Expected: every traversal request is 404 and every control is 200 with a matching hash. Falsifier: any response mixes status or content across request classes. Defense: keep the gate a per-request synchronous computation with no shared mutable state.

evaluations.rationale: Closure is the remaining core: package the repair and run the discriminating robustness suite that folds in every new probe; evidence is already at the regression level.
The open decision point: measure symlink behavior and decide between documenting the limitation and realpath hardening.
Query-string separation is cheap and directly executable, confirming the gate sees only the pathname.
Long-prefix sibling adjacency tests separator-strict comparison; already partially covered, so marginal gain.
Relative-root resolution under a changed working directory is a real configuration variant and cheap to test.
Concurrency is predicted safe because the gate is a per-request synchronous computation; cheap consistency check.

observation.summary: Closure ran against the patched copy. All 18 assertions passed: the full regression set re-passed, query-string variants behaved as predicted (a traversal with a query returned 404 and an ordinary nested file with a query returned 200 with a matching body hash), a sibling directory sharing a long name prefix returned 404, and 20 concurrent requests, half leak attempts and half controls, were fully consistent. A separate run with a relative root under a changed working directory kept the gate effective. Symlink behavior was measured rather than assumed: a directory symlink inside the root served outside content with 200 on both vulnerable and patched copies, while a file symlink returned 500 on both; no marker bytes leaked from the file case. The minimal string-containment repair was retained and the symlink behavior documented as a pre-existing, behavior-preserving limitation. A unified diff and a machine-readable patch record were packaged.
observation.next_hint: The minimal containment repair and its regression evidence are ready. An external official harness must still run the packaged patch; if its hidden tests treat a symlink inside the root as in scope, realpath hardening would be required, otherwise the minimal gate is the recommended repair.
